questions.question: Pointing to a photograph, David said, "She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son." How is the woman in the photo related to David?
questions.explanation: Grandfather's only son is David's father. His daughter is David's sister.

questions.question: Pointing to a man, Sarah says, "His mother is the only daughter of my mother." How is Sarah related to the man?
questions.explanation: The only daughter of Sarah's mother is Sarah herself. So Sarah is his mother.

questions.question: A is B's brother. C is A's father. D is C's father. How is B related to D?
questions.explanation: D is the grandfather of A and B; thus B is D's grandchild.

questions.question: P is the father of Q and R. Q is the son of P, but R is not the son of P. How is R related to P?
questions.explanation: Since R is P's child but not a son, R must be P's daughter.

questions.question: Introducing a man, a woman said, "His wife is the only daughter of my father." How is the man related to the woman?
questions.explanation: The only daughter of the woman's father is the woman herself. Thus the man is her husband.

questions.question: K is the sister of M. J is the mother of M. R is the father of J. How is K related to R?
questions.explanation: J is K's mother and R is J's father, so K is R's granddaughter.

questions.question: Looking at a portrait, Leo said, "Brothers and sisters I have none, but that man's father is my father's son." Whose portrait was it?
questions.explanation: "My father's son" is Leo himself. So "that man's father is Leo", meaning the portrait is of Leo's son.

questions.question: If X is the son of Y's son, how is X related to Y?
questions.explanation: The son of one's son is a grandson.

questions.question: M is the sister of N. P is the father of M. Q is the son of P. How is N related to Q?
questions.explanation: M, N, and Q all share the same father P, making them siblings.

questions.question: A woman points to a boy and says, "His maternal uncle is the maternal uncle of my maternal uncle." How is the boy related to the woman's mother?
questions.explanation: Sharing the same maternal uncle means the boy and the woman's mother are siblings.

questions.question: B is the brother of C. C is the wife of D. E is the son of D. How is B related to E?
questions.explanation: C is E's mother, and B is C's brother, so B is E's maternal uncle.

questions.question: V is the mother of W. W is the sister of X. X is the father of Y. How is V related to Y?
questions.explanation: X is Y's father and V is X's mother, making V the paternal grandmother.

questions.question: G is the daughter of H. H is married to J. J is the father of K. How is G related to K?
questions.explanation: Both G and K are children of H and J, so G is K's sister.

questions.question: T is the son of S. U is the sister of T. V is the daughter of U. How is T related to V?
questions.explanation: T is the brother of V's mother U, so T is maternal uncle.

questions.question: R is the niece of S. S is the sister of T. T is R's mother. How is S related to R?
questions.explanation: S is the sister of R's mother T, making S the maternal aunt.

questions.question: A man said to a lady, "Your mother's husband's sister is my aunt." How is the lady related to the man?
questions.explanation: The lady's mother's husband is her father. His sister is her aunt, the same aunt as the man's.

questions.question: F is the father of G and H. H is married to I. I has a son J. How is F related to J?
questions.explanation: F is the parent of H, who is the parent of J, making F the grandfather.

questions.question: If P $ Q means P is the father of Q, and P # Q means P is the sister of Q, what does A # B $ C mean?
questions.option_a: A is the mother of C
questions.option_b: A is the sister of C
questions.option_c: A is the grandmother of C
questions.option_d: A is the paternal aunt of C
questions.explanation: A is the sister of B, and B is the father of C. Thus A is the paternal aunt of C.

questions.question: E is the son of A. D is the son of B. E is married to C. C is B's daughter. How is D related to E?
questions.explanation: D is the brother of C (E's wife), making D the brother-in-law of E.

questions.question: L is the daughter of M. N is the brother of L. O is the wife of N. How is M related to O?
questions.explanation: M is the parent of O's husband N, making M the parent-in-law.

questions.question: P is Q's brother. R is Q's mother. S is R's father. T is S's mother. How is P related to T?
questions.explanation: T -> S -> R -> P spans three generations down, so P is the great-grandson.

questions.question: A is the son of C; C and Q are sisters; Z is the mother of Q. How is Z related to A?
questions.explanation: C is A's mother and Z is C's mother, so Z is A's maternal grandmother.

questions.question: Pointing to an elderly man, Kunal said, "His son is my son's uncle." How is the elderly man related to Kunal?
questions.explanation: Kunal's son's uncle is Kunal's brother. The elderly man is the father of Kunal's brother, hence Kunal's father.

questions.question: Rahul and Robin are brothers. Pramod is Robin's father. Sheela is Pramod's sister. Preema is Pramod's niece. Shubha is Sheela's granddaughter. How is Rahul related to Shubha?
questions.explanation: Rahul is the son of Pramod, generationally an uncle to Shubha.

questions.question: A is the father of B and C. B is the son of A. But C is not the son of A. How is C related to B?
questions.explanation: C is A's child and not a son, so C is a daughter, making C the sister of B.

questions.question: Pointing to a girl in the park, Amar said, "She is the daughter of the only son of my grandfather." How is the girl related to Amar?
questions.explanation: The grandfather's only son is Amar's father. His daughter is Amar's sister.

questions.question: Deepak said to Nitin, "That boy playing with football is the younger of the two brothers of the daughter of my father's wife." How is the boy related to Deepak?
questions.explanation: Father's wife is Deepak's mother; her daughter is Deepak's sister; her brother is Deepak's brother.

questions.question: Introducing a man to her husband, a woman said, "His brother's father is the only son of my grandfather." How is the woman related to this man?
questions.explanation: His brother's father is his father. The grandfather's only son is her father. So they are siblings.

questions.question: Anil introduces Rohit as the son of the only brother of his father's wife. How is Rohit related to Anil?
questions.explanation: Father's wife is mother. Mother's brother is maternal uncle. Uncle's son is a cousin.

questions.question: Q's mother is sister of P and daughter of M. S is daughter of P and sister of T. How is M related to T?
questions.explanation: M is the parent of P, and P is the parent of T, so M is the grandparent.

questions.question: A person walks 5 km North, turns right and walks 12 km. How far is the person from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Distance = sqrt(5^2 + 12^2) = sqrt(25 + 144) = 13 km.

questions.question: Maya walks 8 km East, then turns left and walks 6 km North. What is the straight-line distance to her start?
questions.explanation: Distance = sqrt(8^2 + 6^2) = 10 km.

questions.question: A cyclist travels 9 km South, turns West and rides 12 km. What is the shortest distance back?
questions.explanation: Distance = sqrt(9^2 + 12^2) = 15 km.

questions.question: Starting facing North, you turn 90 degrees clockwise, then 180 degrees counter-clockwise. Which direction do you face?
questions.explanation: North + 90 deg CW = East. East - 180 deg CCW = West.

questions.question: Facing South, an explorer turns 135 degrees clockwise. Which direction is the explorer facing now?
questions.explanation: South + 135 deg clockwise points towards North-West.

questions.question: A drone flies 20 m West, then turns South and flies 15 m. What is the direct return distance?
Raj walked 10 meters towards East, turned left and walked 5 meters, then turned left again and walked 10 meters. In which direction is he from the starting point?
questions.explanation: East 10m, North 5m, West 10m leaves him 5m directly North of start.

questions.question: Kiran walks 30 meters towards North, turns right and walks 40 meters. What is the straight distance from the origin?
questions.explanation: sqrt(30^2 + 40^2) = 50 meters.

questions.question: Facing West, John turns 45 degrees anti-clockwise and then 180 degrees clockwise. Which direction does he face?
questions.explanation: West - 45 = South-West. South-West + 180 = North-East.

questions.question: A car drives 24 km North, then 7 km East. What is the shortest displacement from the garage?
Sunita walks 15 km South, turns right and walks 8 km. How far is she from her home?

questions.explanation: Rotation is 135 deg clockwise. West + 135 deg clockwise is North-East.

questions.question: A runner goes 12 km North, turns left 5 km, then turns left 12 km. In which direction is the runner relative to start?
questions.explanation: The runner is 5 km directly West of the start point.

questions.question: At sunset, a man is facing a pole. The shadow of the pole fell exactly to his right. Which direction was the man facing?
questions.explanation: At sunset the sun is in the West, so shadows fall East. If East is to his right, he must be facing North.

questions.question: At sunrise, if your shadow falls directly behind you, which direction are you facing?
questions.explanation: At sunrise, sunlight comes from the East and shadows fall to the West. Facing West puts the shadow behind you.

questions.question: An autonomous rover moves 16 m East, turns left and moves 12 m North. What is its Euclidean distance from start?
A courier goes 4 km South, 3 km West, and 4 km North. How far is the courier from the depot?
questions.explanation: South 4 and North 4 cancel out, leaving 3 km West.

questions.question: Starting facing East, you make three successive 90-degree right turns. What direction are you facing?
questions.explanation: East -> South -> West -> North (270 deg clockwise).

questions.question: A hiker walks 10 km South, turns left and walks 10 km, then turns left and walks 10 km. Where is the hiker relative to start?
questions.explanation: South 10, East 10, North 10 lands 10 km East of origin.

questions.question: Ship A is 30 nautical miles West of Port. Ship B is 40 nautical miles North of Port. What is the distance between Ship A and Ship B?
questions.explanation: Distance = sqrt(30^2 + 40^2) = 50 nautical miles.

questions.question: Facing South-West, a compass needle rotates 90 degrees anti-clockwise. Where does it point?
questions.explanation: South-West minus 90 deg CCW is South-East.

questions.question: A truck travels 21 km West and then 20 km North. What is the straight line distance to its dispatch center?
If South-East becomes North, North-East becomes West, what will West become?
questions.explanation: This is a 135 deg counter-clockwise transformation.

questions.question: One morning after sunrise, Suresh was standing facing a pole. The shadow of the pole fell exactly to his right. Which direction was he facing?
questions.explanation: In the morning the sun is in the East, shadows fall West. If West is right, Suresh faces South.

questions.question: A submarine moves 35 km East, then 12 km North. What is the direct vector length from origin?
Walking 6 meters East, then 8 meters South, then 6 meters West leaves you how far from start?
questions.explanation: East 6 and West 6 cancel out, leaving 8 meters South.

questions.question: A golfer hits a ball 40 yards North, then 30 yards West into the hole. What was the direct straight shot distance?
Facing North-East, you turn 180 degrees. What is your new facing direction?
questions.explanation: Opposite of North-East is South-West.

questions.question: A delivery bot moves 24 m North, 10 m East. What is the line-of-sight range to base?
Walk 100 m North, turn right 100 m, turn right 50 m, turn right 100 m. How far and in what direction are you from start?
questions.explanation: Net North displacement = 100 - 50 = 50 m. Net East displacement = 100 - 100 = 0.

questions.question: Statements: All cats are mammals. All mammals are animals. Conclusion: Are all cats animals?
questions.explanation: Transitive property: Cats -> Mammals -> Animals implies all cats are animals.

questions.question: Statements: Some apples are fruits. All fruits are healthy. Conclusion: Are some apples healthy?
questions.explanation: The subset of apples that are fruits must be healthy.

questions.question: Statements: All roses are flowers. No flowers are trees. Conclusion: Can any rose be a tree?
questions.explanation: Since the set of flowers is disjoint from trees, roses (a subset of flowers) cannot be trees.

questions.question: Statements: Some pens are blue. Some blue items are heavy. Conclusion: Are some pens definitely heavy?
questions.explanation: Two particular premises ("Some") do not establish an overlap between pens and heavy items.

questions.question: Statements: All dogs bark. Rover does not bark. Conclusion: Is Rover a dog?
questions.option_c: Rover is definitely not a dog
questions.explanation: By Modus Tollens, failing the necessary condition (barking) means Rover is not a dog.

questions.question: Statements: No birds are fish. All parrots are birds. Conclusion: Which is valid?
questions.explanation: Parrots subset of Birds, Birds disjoint from Fish => Parrots disjoint from Fish.

questions.question: Statements: All squares are rectangles. All rectangles are polygons. Which conclusion is valid?
questions.explanation: Transitive inclusion: Squares -> Rectangles -> Polygons.

questions.question: Statements: Some books are novels. All novels are literature. Which conclusion follows?
questions.explanation: The novels that are books belong to literature.

questions.question: Statements: All metals conduct electricity. Wood does not conduct electricity. What follows?
questions.explanation: Contrapositive of "All metals conduct" is "Non-conductors are not metals".

questions.question: Statements: Some integers are even. All even numbers are divisible by 2. What follows?
questions.explanation: The even integers are divisible by 2.

questions.question: Statements: All diamonds are carbon. All carbon is element. What follows?
questions.explanation: Transitive property confirms diamonds are elements.

questions.question: Statements: No reptiles have feathers. All snakes are reptiles. What follows?
questions.explanation: Snakes are a subset of reptiles, which have no feathers.

questions.question: Statements: All prime numbers greater than 2 are odd. 17 is prime. What follows?
questions.explanation: 17 is prime and > 2, so it must be odd.

questions.question: Statements: All computers need power. Device X does not need power. What follows?
questions.option_d: Device X is not a computer
questions.explanation: Modus Tollens proves Device X is not a computer.

questions.question: Statements: Some cars are electric. All electric vehicles produce zero emissions. What follows?
questions.explanation: The electric cars produce zero emissions.

questions.question: Statements: No mammals lay eggs (simplification). Platypus lays eggs. What follows?
questions.explanation: In formal logic, the instance contradicts the universal statement.

questions.question: Statements: All triangles have 3 angles. Shape S has 4 angles. What follows?
questions.option_c: Shape S is not a triangle
questions.explanation: Contrapositive logic proves Shape S is not a triangle.

questions.question: Statements: All musicians are artists. Some artists are painters. What follows?
questions.explanation: Converse of "All musicians are artists" is "Some artists are musicians".

questions.question: Statements: No prime numbers end in 0 (except none). Number N ends in 0. What follows?
questions.option_a: N is not a prime number
questions.explanation: Any number ending in 0 (with >1 digits) is composite, divisible by 2, 5, 10.

questions.question: Statements: All engineers know math. Alex knows math. What follows?
questions.option_b: Alex may or may not be an engineer (Affirming the Consequent fallacy)
questions.explanation: Knowing math is a necessary condition, not sufficient to prove Alex is an engineer.

questions.question: Statements: If it rains, the grass is wet. The grass is wet. What follows?
questions.option_c: It may or may not have rained (Wetness could be due to sprinklers)
questions.explanation: Affirming the consequent is a formal fallacy.

questions.question: Statements: If it rains, the grass is wet. It did not rain. What follows?
questions.option_d: The grass may still be wet from other sources (Denying the antecedent)
questions.explanation: Denying the antecedent does not prove the consequent is false.

questions.question: Statements: If it rains, the grass is wet. The grass is not wet. What follows?
questions.option_a: It did not rain (Valid Modus Tollens)
questions.explanation: Modus Tollens: Not Q implies Not P.

questions.question: Statements: All planets orbit a star. Mars is a planet. What follows?
questions.option_c: Mars does not orbit a star
questions.explanation: Direct Modus Ponens.

questions.question: Statements: No fish can breathe air directly. Whales breathe air directly. What follows?
questions.explanation: Whales possess a property disjoint from fish.

questions.question: Statements: All conifers are evergreens. Pine is a conifer. What follows?
questions.explanation: Deductive categorization.

questions.question: Statements: Some doctors are surgeons. All surgeons are medical graduates. What follows?
questions.explanation: The surgeon doctors must be medical graduates.

questions.question: Statements: All squares are rhombuses. All rhombuses are parallelograms. What follows?
questions.explanation: Transitive geometric hierarchy.

questions.question: Statements: Every integer is a rational number. Pi is not a rational number. What follows?
questions.explanation: Since Pi is irrational, it cannot be an integer.

questions.question: Statements: All valid arguments with true premises are sound. Argument A is sound. What follows?
questions.option_d: Argument A is valid and has true premises
questions.explanation: By definition of soundness in formal logic.

questions.question: Five friends A, B, C, D, E sit in a row. C is in the middle. A is to the immediate left of C. B is at the extreme right end. Who sits between C and B?
questions.explanation: Row order is: _ , A, C, (D or E), B. Thus D or E sits between C and B.

questions.question: Six people P, Q, R, S, T, U sit in a circle facing the center. P is opposite S. Q is to the immediate right of P. R is to the immediate left of P. Who is opposite Q?
questions.explanation: In a 6-person circle, opposite of immediate right of P is the position opposite Q.

questions.question: In a line of 20 people, Kevin is 7th from the left end. What is his position from the right end?
questions.explanation: Position from right = Total - Left + 1 = 20 - 7 + 1 = 14th.

questions.question: In a class of 45 students, Priya ranks 12th from the top. What is her rank from the bottom?
questions.explanation: Rank from bottom = 45 - 12 + 1 = 34th.

questions.question: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F, G sit facing North. D sits exactly in the center. How many people sit to the left of D?
questions.explanation: With 7 people, the center is the 4th position, leaving 3 to the left.

questions.question: In a race, Tom finished ahead of Sam, but behind Alex. Ben finished ahead of Tom. Who definitely did NOT win the race?
questions.explanation: Both Tom and Sam had runners ahead of them, so Sam and Tom could not have won.

questions.question: Four boxes Red, Blue, Green, Yellow are stacked. Red is above Blue. Green is below Blue. Yellow is on top. Which box is at the bottom?
questions.explanation: Top to bottom order: Yellow, Red, Blue, Green. Bottom is Green.

questions.question: In a queue, Rohan is 9th from front and 16th from back. How many people are in the queue?
questions.explanation: Total = 9 + 16 - 1 = 24 people.

questions.question: Five books M, N, O, P, Q are on a shelf. N is to the right of M. O is to the left of M. Q is to the right of P but left of O. Which book is on the extreme left?
questions.explanation: Order from left to right: P, Q, O, M, N. Extreme left is P.

questions.question: Eight colleagues sit around a square table, 2 on each side. A sits opposite E. B is next to A. Who sits opposite B?
questions.explanation: Across a symmetric square table, each seat has a distinct opposite seat.

questions.question: In a row of 30 girls, when Sita was shifted 4 places to the left, she became 8th from the left end. What was her original position from the right end?
questions.explanation: Original left pos = 8 + 4 = 12th. Right pos = 30 - 12 + 1 = 19th.

questions.question: Among 5 friends, Amy is taller than Beth but shorter than Chloe. Diana is taller than Eric but shorter than Beth. Who is the tallest?
questions.explanation: Height order: Chloe > Amy > Beth > Diana > Eric. Tallest is Chloe.

questions.question: Who is the shortest among the 5 friends (Chloe > Amy > Beth > Diana > Eric)?
questions.explanation: Height order puts Eric at the lowest.

questions.question: Six boxes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 are stacked. Box 1 is at the bottom, Box 6 is at the top. If Box 3 and 5 swap, which box is second from top?
questions.explanation: Original second from top was Box 5. After swap, Box 3 is in that position.

questions.question: A, B, C, D, E sit in a circle. A is between E and C. B is to the right of C. Who is between B and E?
questions.explanation: Circular order is E - A - C - B - D - E. Between B and E sits D.

questions.question: In a row of 50 trees, the 18th tree from the left is marked. What is its index from the right end?
questions.explanation: Index from right = 50 - 18 + 1 = 33rd.

questions.question: If Monday is day 1, what day of the week is day 45?
questions.explanation: 45 mod 7 = 3. Day 1 is Mon, Day 2 is Tue, Day 3 is Wed.

questions.question: If today is Friday, what day of the week will it be after 65 days?
questions.explanation: 65 mod 7 = 2. Friday + 2 days = Sunday -> Fri(5) + 65 = 70 mod 7 = 0 (Sunday/Monday depending on convention; 65 = 9*7 + 2 => Fri + 2 = Sun/Mon).

questions.question: In a circular dining table with 8 chairs, how many chairs are strictly between two people sitting opposite each other on either side?
questions.explanation: In an 8-person circle, opposite seats leave 3 chairs on the left and 3 on the right.

questions.question: Five cars P, Q, R, S, T parked in a row. S is to the right of T. Q is to the left of T but right of P. R is to the right of S. Which car is in the middle?
questions.explanation: Order: P, Q, T, S, R. Middle is T.

questions.question: If January 1st of a non-leap year is a Monday, what day is December 31st of that same year?
questions.explanation: A standard non-leap year has 365 days (52 weeks + 1 day). So Jan 1 and Dec 31 share the same day.

questions.question: In a leap year, if Jan 1 is Wednesday, what day is Dec 31?
questions.explanation: A leap year has 366 days (52 weeks + 2 days), ending one weekday ahead.

questions.question: How many times do the hands of a clock overlap in a 12-hour period?
questions.explanation: Due to relative velocity, hands overlap 11 times every 12 hours (22 times in 24 hours).

questions.question: At what angle are the hands of a clock at 3:30?
At what angle are the hands of a clock at 8:20?
Four runners finish in order. Mark did not finish 1st. Luke finished after Mark. John finished before Luke and before Mark. Who was 1st?
questions.explanation: John finished before both Mark and Luke, taking 1st place.

questions.option_b: A single developer making a typo in code
questions.option_d: An attempt to overwhelm a target server, service, or network with a flood of traffic from multiple compromised distributed botnet systems
questions.explanation: Correct resolution: An attempt to overwhelm a target server, service, or network with a flood of traffic from multiple compromised distributed botnet systems.

questions.question: What is the Principle of Least Privilege (PoLP)?
questions.option_a: A security design rule that every user, process, and program should be granted only the minimum permissions necessary to perform its legitimate function
questions.option_b: Denying all employees access to computers
questions.option_c: Giving all users full administrator root access
questions.explanation: Correct resolution: A security design rule that every user, process, and program should be granted only the minimum permissions necessary to perform its legitimate function.

questions.question: What is a Replay Attack and how is it mitigated in cryptographic network protocols?
questions.option_a: Playing an audio recording in an office
questions.option_b: An attacker captures valid authentication traffic and transmits it again later; mitigated using timestamps, session nonces, and unique message IDs
questions.explanation: Correct resolution: An attacker captures valid authentication traffic and transmits it again later; mitigated using timestamps, session nonces, and unique message IDs.

questions.question: What is a Buffer Overflow attack?
questions.option_a: A hard disk running out of storage space
questions.option_c: Writing more data to a fixed-size memory buffer than it can hold, overwriting adjacent memory (such as return addresses) to execute arbitrary code
questions.option_d: A monitor displaying too many colors
questions.explanation: Correct resolution: Writing more data to a fixed-size memory buffer than it can hold, overwriting adjacent memory (such as return addresses) to execute arbitrary code.

questions.question: What is Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR)?
questions.option_a: Assigning random IP addresses to network routers
questions.option_d: An operating system defense that randomizes the memory addresses of key program areas (stack, heap, libraries) to thwart buffer overflow exploits
questions.explanation: Correct resolution: An operating system defense that randomizes the memory addresses of key program areas (stack, heap, libraries) to thwart buffer overflow exploits.

questions.question: What is a Digital Signature and what security guarantees does it provide?
questions.option_a: A cryptographic hash of data encrypted with the sender's private key, providing authenticity, integrity, and non-repudiation
questions.option_c: A scanned image of a handwritten signature
questions.option_d: A company logo on a website
questions.explanation: Correct resolution: A cryptographic hash of data encrypted with the sender's private key, providing authenticity, integrity, and non-repudiation.

questions.question: What is Non-Repudiation in information security?
questions.option_b: The assurance that a party to a communication or transaction cannot deny the authenticity of their signature or action
questions.explanation: Correct resolution: The assurance that a party to a communication or transaction cannot deny the authenticity of their signature or action.

questions.question: What is Penetration Testing (Ethical Hacking)?
questions.option_b: Testing hardware durability with a hammer
questions.option_c: An authorized simulated cyberattack on a computer system performed to evaluate its security posture and identify vulnerabilities
questions.explanation: Correct resolution: An authorized simulated cyberattack on a computer system performed to evaluate its security posture and identify vulnerabilities.

questions.question: What is a Honeypot in network security?
questions.option_a: A jar of honey stored in a server room
questions.option_c: A tool for cleaning computer screens
questions.option_d: A decoy computer system intended to mimic likely targets of cyberattacks to detect, deflect, or study attacker methods
questions.explanation: Correct resolution: A decoy computer system intended to mimic likely targets of cyberattacks to detect, deflect, or study attacker methods.

questions.question: What is Phishing?
questions.option_a: A social engineering attack where adversaries impersonate legitimate institutions via email or messaging to trick individuals into disclosing sensitive credentials
questions.option_b: Scanning for open ports with Nmap
questions.option_c: Catching fish with a fishing rod
questions.explanation: Correct resolution: A social engineering attack where adversaries impersonate legitimate institutions via email or messaging to trick individuals into disclosing sensitive credentials.

questions.question: What is Ransomware?
questions.option_a: Software purchased with a company credit card
questions.option_b: Malicious software that encrypts a victim's files and demands payment in exchange for the decryption key
questions.explanation: Correct resolution: Malicious software that encrypts a victim's files and demands payment in exchange for the decryption key.

questions.question: What is the role of Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) in TLS handshakes?
questions.option_a: Encrypting data with symmetric keys only
questions.option_c: Ensuring that compromise of a long-term private server key does not compromise past session keys or decrypt past recorded traffic
questions.explanation: Correct resolution: Ensuring that compromise of a long-term private server key does not compromise past session keys or decrypt past recorded traffic.

questions.question: What is a Rootkit in operating systems security?
questions.option_a: The root user password in Linux
questions.option_b: A utility for partitioning hard drives
questions.option_d: Stealthy malicious software designed to hide its presence and grant administrative privileged access to a computer system below OS detection
questions.explanation: Correct resolution: Stealthy malicious software designed to hide its presence and grant administrative privileged access to a computer system below OS detection.

questions.question: What does the OWASP Top 10 represent in cybersecurity?
questions.option_a: A regularly updated consensus document outlining the ten most critical web application security risks and vulnerabilities
questions.option_c: A list of top ten computer manufacturers
questions.option_d: A top 10 list of software programming languages
questions.explanation: Correct resolution: A regularly updated consensus document outlining the ten most critical web application security risks and vulnerabilities.

questions.question: What is a Side-Channel Attack (e.g. Spectre, Meltdown, timing attacks)?
questions.option_a: Attacking a server from the side of the room
questions.option_b: An attack based on information gained from the physical implementation of a computer system (timing, power consumption, acoustic emissions, cache behavior) rather than flaws in the algorithm
questions.explanation: Correct resolution: An attack based on information gained from the physical implementation of a computer system (timing, power consumption, acoustic emissions, cache behavior) rather than flaws in the algorithm.

questions.question: What is Port Scanning used for in network reconnaissance?
questions.option_a: Measuring electrical voltage on network ports
questions.option_b: Plugging USB cables into laptop ports
questions.option_c: Probing a server or host to discover open network ports and identifying active network services and potential vulnerabilities
questions.explanation: Correct resolution: Probing a server or host to discover open network ports and identifying active network services and potential vulnerabilities.

questions.question: What is a Web Application Firewall (WAF)?
questions.option_a: A firewall built into home WiFi routers
questions.option_b: A physical brick wall separating server rooms
questions.option_c: An antivirus program installed on smartphones
questions.option_d: A specialized security appliance or reverse proxy that inspects and filters incoming HTTP/HTTPS traffic to block common web attacks like SQLi, XSS, and CSRF
questions.explanation: Correct resolution: A specialized security appliance or reverse proxy that inspects and filters incoming HTTP/HTTPS traffic to block common web attacks like SQLi, XSS, and CSRF.

Which data structure is most optimal for implementing a priority queue?
questions.explanation: Milestone solution: Binary Heaps offer O(1) peek and O(log N) insertion/extraction for priorities.

questions.question:
[Milestone Assessment 1 - Q7] Review question in Data Structures:
What is the minimum number of queues needed to implement a Stack?
questions.explanation: Milestone solution: Two FIFO queues can emulate a LIFO stack by transferring elements.

questions.question:
[Milestone Assessment 1 - Q8] Review question in Data Structures:
Which self-balancing binary search tree guarantees that no path is more than twice as long as any other?
questions.explanation: Milestone solution: Red-Black tree coloring invariants bound the maximum height to 2 * log2(N + 1).

questions.question:
[Milestone Assessment 1 - Q9] Review question in Data Structures:
In a complete binary tree of height H with N nodes, what is the relationship between height and node count?
questions.explanation: Milestone solution: The height of a complete binary tree is logarithmic with respect to total nodes.

questions.question:
[Milestone Assessment 1 - Q10] Review question in Data Structures:
Which tree traversal visits the left subtree, root node, and then right subtree?
questions.explanation: Milestone solution: In-order traversal visits nodes in (Left, Root, Right) order.

questions.question:
[Milestone Assessment 1 - Q11] Review question in Data Structures:
In an array of size N, what is the time complexity of accessing an element at index i directly?
questions.explanation: Milestone solution: Contiguous memory addressing allows instant O(1) random access.

questions.question:
[Milestone Assessment 1 - Q12] Review question in Data Structures:
Which tree structure is optimized for storing hierarchical routing prefixes and autocomplete dictionary words?
questions.explanation: Milestone solution: Tries store shared string prefixes along common tree edges.

questions.question:
[Milestone Assessment 1 - Q13] Review question in Data Structures:
What is the space complexity of an Adjacency Matrix representing a graph with V vertices?
questions.explanation: Milestone solution: A 2D array of dimensions V x V requires O(V^2) memory.

questions.question:
[Milestone Assessment 1 - Q14] Review question in Data Structures:
Which data structure is used to implement Breadth-First Search (BFS) graph traversal?
questions.explanation: Milestone solution: BFS explores vertices level by level using a FIFO Queue.

questions.question:
[Milestone Assessment 1 - Q15] Review question in Data Structures:
Which data structure is typically used for Depth-First Search (DFS) graph traversal?
questions.explanation: Milestone solution: DFS dives along paths using a LIFO Stack or recursive function frames.

questions.question:
[Milestone Assessment 1 - Q16] Review question in Data Structures:
In a circular queue of capacity K with front and rear pointers, how is the next index computed?
questions.explanation: Milestone solution: Modulo arithmetic wraps the pointer around the fixed array boundary.

questions.question:
[Milestone Assessment 1 - Q17] Review question in Data Structures:
What is the balance factor constraint in an AVL Tree for every node?
questions.explanation: Milestone solution: AVL invariant strictly restricts height difference of subtrees to -1, 0, or +1.

questions.question:
[Milestone Assessment 1 - Q18] Review question in Data Structures:
Which data structure is optimal for finding range sum queries with point updates in O(log N)?
questions.option_d: Fenwick Tree (Binary Indexed Tree) or Segment Tree
questions.explanation: Milestone solution: Binary Indexed Trees and Segment Trees support O(log N) prefix sums and point updates.

questions.question:
[Milestone Assessment 1 - Q19] Review question in Data Structures:
What is the worst-case time complexity of inserting into an unbalanced Binary Search Tree?
questions.explanation: Milestone solution: When items are inserted in sorted order, an unbalanced BST degrades into a linked list of height N.

questions.question:
[Milestone Assessment 1 - Q20] Review question in Data Structures:
Which structure enables finding if two items belong to the same set and merging sets in nearly O(1)?
questions.explanation: Milestone solution: Union-Find with path compression and rank union runs in inverse Ackermann time O(alpha(N)).

questions.question:
[Milestone Assessment 1 - Q21] Review question in Data Structures:
In a Max-Heap, where is the largest key always located?
questions.explanation: Milestone solution: The max-heap property mandates that every parent key is greater than or equal to its children.

questions.question:

What is the number of edges in a connected undirected tree with N vertices?
questions.explanation: Milestone solution: Any tree with N vertices has exactly N - 1 edges and contains no cycles.

questions.question:

questions.question:

questions.question:

What is the maximum number of children a node can have in a binary tree?
questions.explanation: Milestone solution: By definition, binary tree nodes have at most two child nodes (left and right).
